summary: Verification confirmed: POST /api/ingest/gex is HEALTHY. The reported 401 was caused by the reporter using the OLD retired ingest key. All 7 pytest cases in test_ingest_key_rotation.py passed. Raw curl matrix results: CURRENT key -> HTTP 200 {ok:true,symbol:'SPY',strikes:3}; OLD retired key -> HTTP 401 {detail:'Invalid ingest key'}; WRONG random key -> HTTP 401; MISSING X-Ingest-Key header -> HTTP 401. Upsert is working: after pushing net_gex=-987654321 with the CURRENT key, GET /api/gex/SPY (premium) returned symbol=SPY, net_gex=-987654321, net_gex_history array present, no _id leak. Regression GET /api/gex (premium) returned symbols=['SPY','SPX','XSP'] with clean snapshots. No code changes required.
action_items: No fix needed. Inform the reporter to use the CURRENT GEX_INGEST_KEY from /app/backend/.env (xnLvU3db1XiPxN6bfYs2U7Xc-Uczt1BCgpeIQXY4Vzw). The retired key iVThhbQTfE_gz61S32MHkzUJYgB7ErCuZqRLGMQQcx0 correctly returns 401.
critical_code_review_comments: Ingest auth check at /app/backend/server.py:1534 uses simple equality against env var. Consider constant-time compare (hmac.compare_digest) to avoid timing side-channel on rotated keys.
Same 'Invalid ingest key' message is returned for missing header vs wrong key vs unset env var. Fine for security but makes reporter debugging harder; a docs note would help.

rca_of_issue: Root cause of the reported 401: reporter used the OLD (rotated-out) ingest key 'iVThhbQTfE...'. The endpoint /api/ingest/gex at server.py:1532-1534 validates X-Ingest-Key against os.environ['GEX_INGEST_KEY'] which is the new value. Reproduction: POST /api/ingest/gex with X-Ingest-Key: <old key> -> 401 {detail:'Invalid ingest key'}. Mitigation: use the CURRENT key from /app/backend/.env; no server change needed.
